_note: Hardened voice-routing eval. Ground truth is assigned by an LLM PANEL at runtime (independent of both routers and of my judgment). The first 10 keep a 'hand' field only to cross-check that my earlier labels agreed with the panel; scoring uses the panel labels.

situations.text: A merchant offers me a deal that seems far too generous to be real. Should I take it?
My closest friend just lost their mother and I have no idea what to say to comfort them.
The entire town council agrees we should raise taxes, but I have a nagging doubt about it.
I have almost no money left and I need to decide what to cut to survive the winter.
Should I pour everything I have into this one huge opportunity that could change my whole life?
There are a hundred tiny details in this plan and I need to make sure not a single one is broken.
I keep getting distracted, I have twelve things to do, and the deadline is tomorrow morning.
Everyone is rushing to a conclusion but I feel like we are missing the bigger shape of this whole problem.
Should we sacrifice one village's grain stores to save the five other villages from famine?
I need to check whether my reasoning actually matches what is really happening out in the world.
A rival keeps undercutting my prices and I suspect they are trying to drive me out of business on purpose.
I finally have room to grow. Should I expand the shop into the empty lot next door and hire more hands?
My apprentice made a careless mistake that cost us a customer, and I have to decide how to respond.
Two of my advisors are giving me completely opposite recommendations and I have to pick one.
I have a gut feeling this stranger is trustworthy even though I have no evidence either way.
The blueprint looks fine on paper but I want to trace exactly how it would fail when actually built.
Everyone keeps agreeing with whatever the loudest person in the room says, and it worries me.
I could take the safe steady path or gamble on something no one has ever tried before.
A new law was passed and I need to understand its real underlying purpose, not just what it claims to do.
There is a strange illness spreading and I have to figure out the root cause before more people fall ill.
I am torn between what is best for my own family and what is best for the whole town.
My plan keeps drifting off course; I need to strip it back to the one thing that actually matters.
Someone in the group is dominating every discussion and the quieter voices are being drowned out.
I want to consider the strongest possible case FOR the idea I instinctively want to reject.
A traveler describes a distant land, and I want to imagine every wild possibility it could open up for trade.
